st-daisy-johnson.notes: Inhuman via Terrigen Mist (AoS ep 32). Ident null: she goes by Quake, but the show never clearly settles whether the public knows Quake is Daisy Johnson. Accords null: not in Civil War (she refuses to register in Slingshot/AoS S4, but the field is Civil War only). Blip null: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. never addresses the Snap.

st-melinda-may.notes: Human until AoS S7, when Simmons revives her from the stasis pod (with Enoch's tech) and she can feel others' emotions, so Enhanced (outside source). Some would file her as Human. 'The Cavalry' is a nickname, not a codename, so ident null. Blip null: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. never addresses the Snap.

st-leo-fitz.notes: No powers. 'The Doctor' is his Framework alias only. Blip null: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. never addresses the Snap.

st-jemma-simmons.notes: No powers. Blip null: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. never addresses the Snap.

st-mack.notes: No powers. Blip null: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. never addresses the Snap.

st-elena-rodriguez.notes: Inhuman (AoS). The rebound limit is gone by S7, when she gains true super speed (per record). Ident null: Yo-Yo is a nickname and Slingshot her Accords codename, but how public that is is not settled. Accords null by the spec (Civil War only). She does sign the Accords in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Slingshot, as the record says. Blip null: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. never addresses the Snap.

steve-rogers.notes: Erskine's serum (First Avenger). Refuses the Accords (Civil War). Survives the Snap in Wakanda (Infinity War, Endgame).

bucky-barnes.notes: Winter Soldier program (HYDRA's serum, Civil War). Ident Public: his Winter Soldier past was secret, then became public (Civil War, pardoned in Falcon and the Winter Soldier). As of Thunderbolts* he is a congressman and is shown publicly as one of the New Avengers. 'Exposed' would also fit. Accords null: not put to him. Turns to dust (Infinity War).

peggy-carter.notes: No powers. Codebreaker at Bletchley Park (Agent Carter ep 12). Blip null: she dies before it (Civil War). Accords null: dead by the time they are put to anyone.

howard-stark.notes: No powers. Flies Peggy and Steve (First Avenger). Blip null: killed in 1991 (Civil War).

tony-stark.notes: No powers; his abilities come from his armor. Says 'I am Iron Man' publicly (Iron Man). Signs the Accords (Civil War). On Titan during the Snap and survives (Infinity War).

pepper-potts.notes: Injected with Extremis (Iron Man 3) and Tony stabilizes it rather than removing it (Wikipedia plot: 'stabilized'), so Enhanced by the spec's Extremis rule. No Extremis powers are shown after Iron Man 3, so some would file her as Human. Ident null: 'Rescue' is never used as a codename on screen. Survives the Snap and raises Morgan (Endgame).

james-rhodes.notes: No powers. Public as War Machine/Iron Patriot (Iron Man 2, Iron Man 3). Signs the Accords and backs Tony (Civil War). Survives the Snap (Infinity War).

happy-hogan.notes: No powers. Blip null: no title shows or states where he was during the Snap. He appears only after the five years (Endgame), and color character posters are marketing, not on screen. Accords null.

phil-coulson.notes: Human, revived with the alien GH-325 drug (AoS) but given no powers. He briefly hosts the Ghost Rider (AoS ep 88). The season 7 Coulson is an LMD (robot) with his memories; the record treats the man as dead by then. Aliases are covers, not codenames. Blip null: the show never addresses the Snap, and he dies around it. Accords null: dead in film continuity during Civil War.

nick-fury.notes: No powers. Turns to dust after paging Carol (Infinity War) and is restored (Endgame). Accords null: not part of the Civil War vote.

jarvis.notes: Tony's AI. His code helps create Vision (Age of Ultron). In VisionQuest (Oct 2026) he lives in Vision's mind and is deleted in episode 2 (web-confirmed). Blip null: AI, and gone as J.A.R.V.I.S. before the Snap.

friday.notes: Tony's AI from Age of Ultron on. Reads Steve's fighting pattern (Civil War) and runs the time-travel simulation (Endgame). Blip null: the Snap targets living beings; she is shown working after it (Endgame). Her VisionQuest episodes follow the record; I confirmed she is in VisionQuest (Orla Brady) but not her per-episode details.

dum-e-and-u.notes: Tony's workshop robots (Iron Man, Iron Man 2). Blip null: not living, and no title says.

bruce-banner.notes: Gamma radiation (The Incredible Hulk), so Enhanced. Publicly known as the Hulk; in Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026) he is a university physics professor whose students ask about his Avengers past (web-confirmed). Survives the Snap (Infinity War) and reverses it (Endgame). Accords null: absent from Civil War. Record note: sources disagree on whether Jean Grey controls the Hulk in Brand New Day or only breaks his inhibitor.

thor.notes: Asgardian prince. Survives the Snap in Wakanda (Infinity War). Ident null: Thor is his name. Accords null: absent from Civil War.

erik-selvig.notes: No powers. His photo is among the missing at the Avengers Compound (Endgame), which agrees with the record.

heimdall.notes: Blip null: Thanos kills him before the Snap (Infinity War).

loki.notes: Frost Giant by birth, raised Asgardian (Thor). The variant in Loki learns to time slip (Loki S2). Blip null: the main Loki dies before the Snap (Infinity War), and the variant is taken from 2012.

clint-barton.notes: No powers. Ident Public as Hawkeye (Hawkeye), but his Ronin identity stays secret from the public (only Kate, Maya and Yelena learn it). Accords null: retired and never put to him in Civil War. Not blipped: his family vanishes and he becomes Ronin (Endgame).

maria-hill.notes: No powers. Turns to dust beside Fury (Infinity War).

natasha-romanoff.notes: Red Room trained, no powers (Black Widow). Public as Black Widow after the S.H.I.E.L.D. data dump and Congress (Winter Soldier). Signs the Accords (Civil War). Survives the Snap (Infinity War, Endgame).

wanda-maximoff.notes: Enhanced follows the spec's example: HYDRA's Mind Stone experiments. WandaVision says she was born with magic as the Scarlet Witch, so Witch is arguable. Does not sign; held at the Compound, then sides with Steve (Civil War). Turns to dust (Infinity War).

vision.notes: Synthezoid body built from Ultron's design and J.A.R.V.I.S.'s code (Age of Ultron). Backs the Accords with Tony (Civil War). Blip null: Thanos kills him moments before the Snap (Infinity War). He loses the Mind Stone; the rebuilt white Vision (WandaVision) returns in VisionQuest (Oct 2026, web-confirmed). Ident null: Vision is his name.

peter-quill.notes: Half human, half Celestial (Ego, Vol. 2). He loses the Celestial power when Ego dies, so Human is also arguable. Star-Lord is openly his name. Turns to dust on Titan (Infinity War).

gamora.notes: Zehoberei, adopted by Thanos. Blip null: sacrificed on Vormir before the Snap (Infinity War). The 2014 variant comes from the past (Endgame).

drax.notes: Turns to dust on Titan (Infinity War). Ident null: 'the Destroyer' is a title, not a secret identity.

rocket.notes: A raccoon uplifted by the High Evolutionary's experiments (Vol. 3), so Enhanced under the experiments rule. He also has cybernetic implants, so Cyborg is arguable. Survives the Snap in Wakanda (Infinity War).

groot.notes: Flora colossus. Turns to dust (Infinity War).

yondu.notes: Centaurian. Blip null: dies before it (Vol. 2).

nebula.notes: Turned into a cyborg by Thanos's modifications. Survives the Snap on Titan (Infinity War, Endgame).

kraglin.notes: Never named on screen; James Gunn said off screen that he is Xandarian. So Alien is not strictly settled by the titles. Inherits Yondu's arrow (Vol. 2). Blip null: no title says.

cosmo.notes: An Earth (Soviet) space dog with psionic powers (Holiday Special, Vol. 3). The titles don't clearly explain where the powers came from; Enhanced assumes an outside source. Blip null: no title says.

mantis.notes: Alien, raised by Ego. The Holiday Special reveals she is Peter's half-sister through Ego, so she is half Celestial too; Alien is kept for her unnamed other species. Turns to dust on Titan (Infinity War).

carol-danvers.notes: Powers from the Tesseract-powered engine blast (Captain Marvel). Survives the Snap and attends the five-years-later meeting (Endgame). Accords null: not in Civil War.

monica-rambeau.notes: Powers from crossing the Hex barrier (WandaVision). Returns from the Blip (WandaVision ep 4). No codename on screen.

trevor-slattery.notes: Actor with no powers. Ident null: the Mandarin is a role he plays, not a secret identity (exposed as a fake in Iron Man 3, revived as a cover in Wonder Man). Wonder Man (2026, web-confirmed): he spies on Simon for Damage Control, claims the blast as the Mandarin, is imprisoned, and is broken out. Blip null: no title says.

sam-wilson.notes: No powers. Publicly Falcon, then Captain America (Falcon and the Winter Soldier). Rejects the Accords (Civil War). Turns to dust (Infinity War).

scott-lang.notes: No powers; his size changes come from the suit. Publicly Ant-Man (Quantumania). Accords null: never put to him; he is arrested for breaking them (Civil War). Not blipped: trapped in the Quantum Realm during the Snap (Ant-Man and the Wasp), though a memorial wrongly lists him among the vanished (Endgame).

hope-van-dyne.notes: No powers; her abilities come from the suit. Turns to dust (Ant-Man and the Wasp). Ident null: no title settles whether the public knows she is the Wasp.

cassie-lang.notes: No powers. Five years older when Scott returns (Endgame). Builds the Quantum Realm signal device and her own suit (Quantumania).

ghost.notes: Powers from a quantum lab accident (Ant-Man and the Wasp). Ident Public: at the end of Thunderbolts* (web-confirmed), Valentina presents the team at a press conference as the New Avengers. Blip null: no title says.

tchalla.notes: The heart-shaped herb gives him his powers (Black Panther), so Enhanced under the outside-source rule. Publicly king and Black Panther. Accords null: his father signs in Vienna, but they are not put to T'Challa himself (Civil War). Turns to dust (Infinity War).

ayo.notes: No powers. Blip null: fights in Wakanda (Infinity War), but no title says whether she survived.

helmut-zemo.notes: No powers. 'Baron' is a noble title, not a codename, so ident null. Blip null: Falcon and the Winter Soldier doesn't say.

shuri.notes: Takes her synthetic heart-shaped herb and becomes Black Panther (Wakanda Forever). Shown among the lost and back after five years (Endgame). Ident null: no title settles whether the world knows she is the new Black Panther.

okoye.notes: No powers. Works with the Avengers in the five years after the Snap (Endgame).

nakia.notes: Wakandan War Dog spy (Black Panther). Blip null: Wakanda Forever has her living in Haiti raising Toussaint but never says whether she was dusted; she does not appear in Infinity War or Endgame.

m-baku.notes: Jabari leader, no powers. Not blipped: he is still standing in Wakanda after the Snap at the end of Infinity War.

ramonda.notes: No powers or notable combat skills; queen is a role, not an ability. Not blipped: in Endgame's closing scenes she is reunited with her returned children T'Challa and Shuri, which matches the record ('welcomes T'Challa home after the Blip is undone').

yelena-belova.notes: Red Room training, no serum, so Human. Codename: Black Widow, taken from Natasha (Brand New Day, 2026, confirmed). Public: Valentina presents her team to the press as the New Avengers in Thunderbolts* (2025, confirmed). Blipped: Hawkeye episode 5 opens in 2018 with Yelena dusting and coming back five years later.

alexei-shostakov.notes: Red Guardian is the Soviet super soldier from the Red Room (Black Widow). Ident Public because Valentina unveils him to the press as one of the New Avengers (Thunderbolts*, 2025, confirmed). No title says whether the world knew Alexei was Red Guardian before that. Blip null: he is in a Russian prison in 2016, and his blip status is never stated.

peter-parker.notes: Powers from a spider bite. Ident: unmasked by Mysterio at the end of Far From Home, then forgotten after Strange's spell in No Way Home. He is still forgotten in Brand New Day (2026, confirmed): MJ and Ned don't remember him, and he reintroduces himself to Ned with their handshake. Accords null: in Civil War Tony recruits him, but the Accords are never put to him on screen. Blipped: Infinity War, on Titan.

may-parker.notes: No powers. Blipped: Far From Home (record agrees). Dies in No Way Home. In Brand New Day (2026, confirmed) she appears only in a memory Peter shares with Jean Grey.

ned-leeds.notes: Idx Human with a caveat: Ned opens portals with Strange's sling ring in No Way Home, but he is not a trained sorcerer and the titles give him no other power. Blipped: Far From Home, with the Midtown students. Brand New Day (2026, confirmed): he built a 'Spidey Tracker' app and Peter reintroduces himself with their handshake.

flash-thompson.notes: No powers or notable skills. Blipped: Far From Home, with the Midtown students (record agrees).

stephen-strange.notes: Trained Master of the Mystic Arts. Ident null: 'Doctor Strange' is his own name and title, not a codename or masked identity. Accords null: he is not in Civil War. Blipped: Infinity War, on Titan. Dreamwalking: Multiverse of Madness.

wong.notes: Master of the Mystic Arts, later Sorcerer Supreme. Not blipped: in No Way Home, Strange says Wong got the Sorcerer Supreme title only because Strange was gone (blipped) for five years. That tells us Wong was still here, though nobody says it in so many words.

billy-maximoff.notes: Idx Witch, as the spec says (Agatha All Along). Telepathy: WandaVision episode 7. Soul transference: he puts Tommy's soul into a drowning boy (Agatha All Along). Dream-binding: VisionQuest (2026, confirmed by finale coverage). Ident null: he is never shown going by 'Wiccan' as a public codename. Blip null: born after it. Record check: Wikipedia's VisionQuest summary says Tommy and Vision later visit Billy in 'Eastview'. That doesn't clearly contradict the record's 'reaches England' step, but the episode-8 wording of the record's steps is worth a second look.

tommy-maximoff.notes: Idx null: no title says what he is. He was made by Wanda's magic in WandaVision, then his soul was put into Thomas Shepherd (Agatha All Along). VisionQuest (2026) shows his powers (super-speed, phasing, energy redirection) but never explains where they come from or calls him a witch or a mutant. Ident null: no codename. Blip null: born after it. Record check: Wikipedia says Paladin captures Thomas Shepherd in episode 1, while the record puts the capture in episode 2. Please check the episode numbers.

agatha-harkness.notes: Witch (spec example). Power absorption: she drains other witches' power (Agatha All Along). 'Agnes' is a cover persona, not a codename, so ident is null. Blip null: never stated in her listed title. She ends as a ghost (record: Deceased).

john-walker.notes: He takes the Power Broker's serum (FATWS episode 5). Ident Public: he is publicly Captain America, then U.S. Agent, and is unveiled as one of the New Avengers (Thunderbolts*, 2025, confirmed). Blip null: never stated.

kate-bishop.notes: No powers. Ident Public, with medium confidence: she takes the name Hawkeye and never hides her face, but no title says outright that the world knows. Blip null: never stated in Hawkeye or The Marvels.

america-chavez.notes: Idx null: Multiverse of Madness never says what she is or where her power comes from. She has had it since she was a child and comes from another universe, so neither Human nor Enhanced fits for certain. Ident null: no codename. Blip null: from another universe, and never stated.

sersi.notes: Blip null for all the Eternals: the film never says on screen whether any were dusted. Director Chloé Zhao said in interviews that they were exempt, but that is outside the titles.

thena.notes: Blip null: see the Sersi note (not stated on screen).

kingo.notes: He fires energy blasts from his hands. Blip null: see the Sersi note.

phastos.notes: He builds the Uni-Mind device. Blip null: see the Sersi note.

makkari.notes: Blip null: see the Sersi note.

druig.notes: He controls minds, including whole villages. Blip null: see the Sersi note.

gilgamesh.notes: Blip null: see the Sersi note.

ajak.notes: Prime Eternal. Blip null: see the Sersi note.

shang-chi.notes: No innate powers; his power comes from the Ten Rings. 'Shaun' is a name he lived under, not a codename, so ident is null. Blip null: the film references the Blip but never says whether he was dusted.

marc-spector.notes: Idx Enhanced, because his powers come from an outside source (he is the avatar of the god Khonshu). Ident Secret: the public never learns who Moon Knight is (Layla and the Egyptian gods know). Blip null: never stated.

jack-russell.notes: Ident null: 'Werewolf by Night' is the special's title, not a codename he uses. His curse is revealed only to the hunters at the Bloodstone manor, not to the world, so the Exposed/Secret terms don't clearly apply. Blip null: never stated.

elsa-bloodstone.notes: No powers. Blip null: never stated.

adam-warlock.notes: Idx Alien: he is an artificial being made by the Sovereign, and the list has no term of its own for that. Ability details are confirmed only by secondary sources. Blip null: never stated.

kamala-khan.notes: Mutant: Ms. Marvel says so (spec example). Ident Secret, with medium confidence: her family and allies know, and so does Damage Control in the Ms. Marvel finale. Neither title shows the wider public knowing that Kamala is Ms. Marvel, and Marvel.com lists her identity as secret. Blip null: never stated.

riri-williams.notes: No innate powers. At the end of Ironheart (2025, confirmed) Mephisto's veins spread up her arm, but no new power is shown. Ident null: Ironheart never settles whether the public knows Riri is the armored hero. Blip null: never stated in Ironheart (confirmed) or Wakanda Forever.

bob.notes: Idx Enhanced: O.X.E.'s Project Sentry experiment gave him his powers (Thunderbolts*, 2025, confirmed). Some summaries call it a version of the super-soldier serum, but it is not one of the serums the spec lists, hence medium confidence. Ident Public: Valentina presents him to the press as the Sentry and one of the New Avengers. The Void traps people in their worst memories. Blip null: never stated.

wolverine.notes: Idx Mutant: Deadpool & Wolverine calls him a mutant, and I took the spec's mention of D&W as including him. Ident null: he goes by Wolverine, but the film never settles whether the public knows who he is, either on his home world or on Wade's. Blip null: he is a variant from another universe.

reed-richards.notes: Cosmic rays. On Earth-828 the Fantastic Four are public celebrities (First Steps, 2025, confirmed). Blip null: another universe.

sue-storm.notes: Cosmic rays. Public celebrity on Earth-828. She dies and Franklin revives her (confirmed). Blip null: another universe.

johnny-storm.notes: Cosmic rays. Public celebrity on Earth-828. He deciphers the Silver Surfer's language (confirmed). Blip null: another universe.

ben-grimm.notes: Cosmic rays. Public celebrity on Earth-828. Blip null: another universe.

st-matt-murdock.notes: Senses heightened by a chemical accident. Ident Exposed: in the Born Again S2 finale ('The Southern Cross', 2026, confirmed) he publicly reveals in court that he is Daredevil, then is arrested and jailed, which matches the record. Blip null: never stated.

st-karen-page.notes: No powers. Ab null: she is an investigative reporter, which is a profession, not an ability. Born Again S2 (confirmed): the judges dismiss her case. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-foggy-nelson.notes: No powers. Lawyer (not an ability). Killed by Bullseye in Born Again S1 episode 1; the S2 appearance is a flashback (episode 5, the McCoy case, confirmed). Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-claire-temple.notes: No powers. Ab null: nursing is a profession, and her dojo training with Colleen is too slight to list. 'Night Nurse' is a nickname, not a masked identity, so ident is null. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-brett-mahoney.notes: NYPD officer, by Born Again S2 Chief of Detectives (confirmed). No powers. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-mitchell-ellison.notes: Editor at the New York Bulletin. No powers. Born Again S2: in the finale the Bulletin hires BB Urich (confirmed). Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-josie.notes: Bar owner. No powers. Born Again S2 episode 2: the anti-vigilante task force raids her bar (confirmed). Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-jessica-jones.notes: Powers from IGH experiments (Jessica Jones S2). Ident null: she uses her own name and no codename. Born Again S2 (2026, confirmed): she fights the task force with Matt and reunites with Luke; they have a daughter, Danielle. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-luke-cage.notes: Powers from the Seagate experiment. Ident null: he is publicly known as Luke Cage, has no mask and is never called Power Man as a codename on screen; Carl Lucas is his birth name. Born Again S2 (confirmed): he is back from CIA work overseas for Mr. Charles. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-trish-walker.notes: Powers from Malus's procedure (Jessica Jones S2). Ident null: in S3 she is a masked vigilante and is arrested and sent to the Raft, but I found no source saying the public learns she was the vigilante, so Secret and Exposed are both unsettled. 'Hellcat' is never used as her name on screen. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-jeri-hogarth.notes: Lawyer, no powers. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-danny-rand.notes: Idx Enhanced, with medium confidence: the Iron Fist is a power gained from outside (Shou-Lao in K'un-Lun) that can pass to others, and Davos and Colleen both take it in Iron Fist S2. Sorcerer would be a stretch. Ident null: 'Iron Fist' is a title he claims openly, never a masked identity, and the titles never say whether the public knows him by it. At the end of S2 he channels chi through his guns. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

st-frank-castle.notes: No powers. Ident Public: his trial in Daredevil S2 makes it public that he is the Punisher, and he remains openly the Punisher through The Punisher: One Last Kill (2026, confirmed: the Gnucci family) and Brand New Day (2026, confirmed: he shoots at Jean Grey and hits Peter). Blip null: never stated.

st-thembi-wallace.notes: TV reporter, no powers. Blip: never shown or stated in this person's titles.

red-skull.notes: Took an early version of Erskine's serum (The First Avenger), so Super soldier per the spec. Red Skull is his name in the record, not a hidden identity, so ident null. Blip null: Infinity War and Endgame show him on Vormir but never say whether the Snap took him. Not part of the Accords.

obadiah-stane.notes: Ordinary human who builds and pilots the Iron Monger suit and paralyzes Tony with a sonic device (Iron Man). Iron Monger is a suit, not a hidden identity. Died in 2008, so blip null.

ivan-vanko.notes: Builds his own arc reactor and whip harness, then reprograms Hammer's drones (Iron Man 2). Whiplash is a press-style name, not a hidden identity. Died in 2010, so blip null.

emil-blonsky.notes: idx: The Incredible Hulk doses him first with a super soldier serum from Ross's program, then with Banner's blood, which makes him the Abomination. His powers now come from the gamma/blood transformation, so Enhanced. Super soldier is arguable, which is why conf is medium. She-Hulk shows him changing at will. Abomination is not a hidden identity. Blip null: no title says whether he was dusted (he was in prison). Not part of the Accords.

thaddeus-ross.notes: idx: in Captain America: Brave New World (confirmed by search) Ross turns into Red Hulk because Samuel Sterns spiked his pills with gamma, so Enhanced. Accords null: he drafted and pushed the Accords in Civil War but was never asked to sign them. Blip null: the fan wiki says he was dusted and came back, but I found no on-screen line, and Endgame only shows him at the funeral. Red Hulk is not a codename he hides behind; it happened in public in Washington. Abilities kept to what is clearly shown; some write-ups mention heat building with his anger, but I left that out as unconfirmed.

thanos.notes: idx: a Titan, a species not on the list. The MCU never calls him an Eternal (Eternals only calls Eros 'brother to Thanos'), so Alien. Blip: Not blipped, since Infinity War shows him surviving his own snap and Endgame opens with him alive in the Garden. The 2014 variant's dusting in Endgame is not the Snap.

malekith.notes: A Dark Elf of Svartalfheim (Thor: The Dark World). Not a listed species, so Alien. Died in 2013, so blip null.

ronan.notes: Kree Accuser (Captain Marvel, Guardians of the Galaxy). Puts the Power Stone in his Universal Weapon. Died in 2014, so blip null.

ego.notes: In Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 Ego says outright that he is a Celestial. Died in 2014, so blip null.

yon-rogg.notes: Kree Starforce commander (Captain Marvel, set in 1995). He only ever appears there, so blip null since no title says what happened to him at the Snap. Conf medium only because his abilities are thin: mostly combat skill and command.

supreme-intelligence.notes: The Kree's ruling AI. In Captain Marvel it appears to Carol as the person she admires most and holds her back through her implant. The Marvels says Carol destroyed it. Not a living being, and no title ties it to the Snap, so blip null.

aldrich-killian.notes: idx: Enhanced by Extremis (Iron Man 3). ident null on purpose: he secretly is 'the Mandarin' behind Trevor Slattery, but no title settles whether the world ever learned it was Killian. All Hail the King and Shang-Chi only say the Mandarin was faked. So I couldn't choose between Secret and Exposed. Died in 2013, so blip null.

alexander-pierce.notes: An ordinary human politician and HYDRA leader with no special abilities shown, so ab null. Died in 2014 (The Winter Soldier), so blip null. Not part of the Accords.

jasper-sitwell.notes: An ordinary S.H.I.E.L.D. agent (and HYDRA mole) with no notable abilities, so ab null. Died in 2014, so blip null. Conf medium because the record has two likely errors. (1) The HYDRA academy flashback with Hale is Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 5 episode 15, 'Rise and Shine' (515), not 'episode 103'. (2) Simmons catches/stuns Sitwell at the Hub in S1E7 'The Hub' (107). His leaving for the Lemurian Star comes later in season 1 (around E16, 'End of the Beginning'), so the 'episode 16' step mixes two episodes.

ultron.notes: An AI born from the Mind Stone (Age of Ultron). VisionQuest (2026) was checked by search: episode 8 matches the record (Jocasta frees him into her nanobots, he builds a body, kills Virgil, threatens London, is talked down by Vision, and survives in stray nanobots). Blip null: destroyed in 2015, and VisionQuest doesn't tie him to the Snap. Conf medium because the VisionQuest details come from recaps, not from watching it.

darren-cross.notes: idx: human in Ant-Man. In Quantumania Kang rebuilds him as M.O.D.O.K., his head in a mechanical war body, so Cyborg as of his latest title. ident Secret: no title shows the public learning that Cross was Yellowjacket, and he vanished into the Quantum Realm, but that is from absence, not a stated fact. Blip null: he was lost in the Quantum Realm, and nothing is said. Conf medium for both idx and ident.

dreykov.notes: Ordinary human who controls the Widows chemically and is protected by a pheromone lock (Black Widow, set in 2016). Dead before the Snap, so blip null.

valentina.notes: An ordinary human spymaster and politician; ab null. Thunderbolts* (checked by search): facing impeachment, she covers up the Sentry/Void disaster by announcing the team as the New Avengers, and survives. That matches the record. Blip null: no title says whether she was dusted. Not part of the Accords.

killmonger.notes: idx: in Black Panther he takes the heart-shaped herb, which gives him powers from an outside source, so Enhanced. Killmonger is a nickname, not a hidden identity. Died in 2016, so blip null. Eyes of Wakanda (2025, checked by search): the finale 'The Last Panther' ends with a silent Killmonger in the London museum before the axe, which matches the record.

vulture.notes: ident: he flew as the Vulture in secret, then in Homecoming Spider-Man leaves him at the crash and he goes to prison for it. In the mid-credits scene Gargan knows he is tied to Spider-Man. So Exposed, but nothing on screen shows the public being told, hence conf medium. Morbius (in the record, and outside the MCU proper) leaves him without an identity in another universe and doesn't change this. Blip null: he was in prison and the Snap is never mentioned.

hela.notes: Odin's firstborn (Thor: Ragnarok). Raises the Berserkers and Fenris. Died in 2017, before the Snap, so blip null.

he-who-remains.notes: A 31st-century human scientist by his own account (Loki S1 finale). He lives at the Citadel at the End of Time, outside the Snap, so blip null. Conf medium: his abilities are described rather than shown (he dodges Sylvie's blade, knows what will be said, and uses TemPads).

arishem.notes: Prime Celestial (Eternals). Blip null: never stated, and he is a cosmic entity.

dar-benn.notes: Kree leader (The Marvels). Blip null: never stated.

Record note: the Red Room rescue is S2E5 (overall ep 14), not ep 18, though the step bundles it with S2E9 events.

by-starlord-tchalla.notes: Taken from Wakanda as a child by Yondu's Ravagers, so he never takes the heart-shaped herb: Human, no powers (What If...? S1E2). Ident Public: he is the galaxy's famous outlaw Star-Lord and makes no secret that he is T'Challa. Persuasion: he talks Thanos out of his plan. Medium only because the ab list is a judgment call. Blip null: in his universe Thanos gives up his plan, so there is no Snap.

by-the-watcher.notes: Idx is a judgment call: the Watchers are a race outside time and space, closer to Dormammu-level beings than to an ordinary off-world species, so Cosmic being rather than Alien. Cameos all confirmed by search: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man finale (as Strange says goodbye), Eyes of Wakanda ep 4 (in the sky over Adwa, 1896), and Daredevil: Born Again S2 ep 4 'Gloves Off' (an outline in Fogwell's Gym's broken window, which Brad Winderbaum teased with 'always watching'). Ident and blip null.

by-kahhori.notes: A Mohawk woman whose powers come from the Tesseract-touched lake (What If...? S2E6), so Enhanced under the outside-source rule. Season 3 finale (checked by search): Uatu has Carter's team take the Watchers' oath, Kahhori gains Watcher powers, and she is asked to watch over the multiverse. That could make her Cosmic being, but the show doesn't say she stops being herself, so I kept Enhanced. Ident and blip null.

by-zombie-kamala.notes: Idx left null. Her 616 version is Mutant (Ms. Marvel), but the addendum says to ground this in Marvel Zombies alone, and I couldn't confirm that the series calls her a mutant or explains her powers. Mutant is the likely value if it does. Ab from recaps (checked): a hard-light bubble saves the group in the ocean, she shields against Namor and kills him by enlarging a hard-light hand inside his mouth, and a failing force field on re-entry. Ident null: the series never settles who knows she is Ms. Marvel. Finale matches the record: she takes Wanda's hand and wakes in an illusion. Blip null.

by-zombie-riri.notes: No powers. Bitten in episode 1, she seems lost (record: Missing). In the finale (checked) she is alive and armed and breaks into Wanda's illusion to tell Kamala it isn't real. How she survived (an antidote, or F.R.I.D.A.Y. pulling her out) is not settled on screen, so it is not listed as an ability. Ident null: never settled. Blip null.

by-blade-knight.notes: An Eric Brooks variant who became Khonshu's avatar after Moon Knight died in the plague; he tells Kamala this, and Khonshu (F. Murray Abraham) comes out of him at New Asgard's gates (checked by search). Idx Vampire, following the addendum's half-vampire Blade, and coverage calls him a vampire-human hybrid and daywalker. Medium because I couldn't find a recap that describes a clear on-screen vampire moment. Dies in the finale to zombie Thor's lightning/Bifrost blast, which matches the record. Ident null: 'Blade' is the name he goes by, with no public or secret identity in play. Blip null.

by-zombie-yelena.notes: Red Room training, no serum, so Human, as for her 616 file. Hacking: she hacks her way in to chase Zemo (ep 2 recap, checked). Dies staying on the Raft to override the escape pod's launch, which matches the record. Ident null: Marvel Zombies never settles a Black Widow identity for her. Blip null.

by-zombie-shang-chi.notes: No innate powers, as for his 616 file. Ep 2 (checked): bitten in the San Francisco outbreak, he gets the Ten Rings from Wenwu, who dies, to keep the infection from spreading past his arm. Five years on he shares the rings with Katy. Record check: the record says the infection takes him in Paris and he turns. The finale recap I read says he is killed in Paris alongside Rintrah as Wanda siphons Thor's power, and it doesn't show him turning, so the 'turns into a zombie' wording may be worth a second look. 'Shaun' is not a codename, so ident null. Blip null.

pr-mister-fantastic.notes: Powers from the cosmic storm on Doom's station (Fantastic Four 2005). Ident Public: the Four are celebrities, Johnny gives them their codenames in public, and Rise of the Silver Surfer centers on their media-circus wedding. Blip null: another universe with no Snap.

pr-invisible-woman.notes: Powers from the cosmic storm (Fantastic Four 2005). Public, like the rest of the Four. In Rise of the Silver Surfer she dies shielding the Surfer with a force field and he revives her, which matches the record. Blip null.

pr-human-torch.notes: Cosmic-storm powers (Fantastic Four 2005). Power swapping: after touching the Surfer he swaps powers with whoever he touches, then takes on all four to beat Doom (Rise of the Silver Surfer). Public celebrity. Deadpool & Wolverine: this is Chris Evans's Fox Johnny in the Void, whom Cassandra Nova kills, as the record says. Blip null.

pr-the-thing.notes: Turned to rock by the cosmic storm (Fantastic Four 2005). Public: his form can't be hidden, and he is publicly 'The Thing' of the famous Four. Blip null.

pr-silver-surfer.notes: From another world: he tells Sue he serves Galactus to spare his own world and the woman he loves (Rise of the Silver Surfer). Alien, but his powers come from Galactus, so Enhanced is a defensible reading. He revives Sue. His name is never given in the film and he has no secret identity, so ident null. Blip null. Record check: the first step (turning on Galactus and drifting in space) repeats the film's ending ahead of the earlier steps. Not wrong, but it is out of order.

pr-blade.notes: Half-vampire Daywalker (Blade trilogy; Blade: The Series), the addendum's own example of Vampire. Ident null and the reason for medium: 'Blade' is the name he lives by, not a masked identity, and no title settles a public or secret identity. Trinity has the FBI hunting him by that name. Deadpool & Wolverine: Snipes's Blade fights in the Void, as the record says. Blip null.

pr-abraham-whistler.notes: No powers. Bitten by Frost's vampires (Blade), he turns up in Blade II as a vampire captive, and Blade cures him, so he files as Human. He dies in the FBI raid (Blade: Trinity). Ident and blip null.

A mystic discipline could be read as Sorcerer-like, so medium. Revived by Stick, as the record says. Deadpool & Wolverine: in the Void. Ident and blip null.

pr-punisher.notes: No powers. An FBI agent and ex-special forces in The Punisher (2004). There's been like five', so the film leaves open which Punisher died. pr-st-chase-stein.notes: No powers. He builds his gear himself (Runaways). Ident and blip null.

fox-yashida.notes: An old, dying industrialist with no powers of his own; the armor's blade cuts off Logan's claws and its machine starts draining Logan's healing (The Wolverine). fox-sebastian-shaw.notes: X-Men: First Class: absorbs kinetic and nuclear energy and fires it back, has barely aged between 1944 and 1962, and wears a helmet that blocks Xavier. Klaus Schmidt is a past alias, not a codename, so ident null. Accords and blip null per the addendum (no Civil War, no Snap in these titles).

fox-emma-frost.notes: X-Men: First Class shows her reading and bending minds and turning to diamond. fox-azazel.notes: X-Men: First Class shows him teleporting himself and others (Shaw, Erik's band). Accords and blip null per the addendum (no Civil War, no Snap in these titles).

Accords and blip null per the addendum (no Civil War, no Snap in these titles).

fox-bolivar-trask.notes: Days of Future Past: human scientist who experiments on mutants and designs the Sentinels. No codename, so ident null. Accords and blip null per the addendum (no Civil War, no Snap in these titles).

Accords and blip null per the addendum (no Civil War, no Snap in these titles).

Accords and blip null per the addendum (no Civil War, no Snap in these titles).

Accords and blip null per the addendum (no Civil War, no Snap in these titles).

sv-carjacker-2002.notes: Ordinary thief with no powers or codename. Spider-Man 3 gives his name, Dennis Carradine, and says he was the accomplice while Flint Marko fired the shot. Accords null (addendum: never used outside Civil War). Blip null: no Snap in these titles.

A bony plate guards his heart, so Blade's blade can't pierce it from the front. He kills himself with Blade's sword, as in the record.

The sources I checked don't say whether he was born or turned; either way he is a Vampire. pr-bullseye.notes: Daredevil (2003): no stated powers, just inhuman accuracy with anything he throws (paper clips, shuriken, peanuts). Ident null: the film gives him only the codename, with no civilian name or identity whose status could be judged.

So idx is null: Human, Enhanced or Sorcerer would all be guesses. Abilities kept to what is shown: swordplay and martial arts.

pr-howard-saint.notes: The Punisher (2004): a Tampa crime boss and money launderer with no powers. Ab null: running a crime family is not an ability.

by-strange-supreme.notes: A trained Master of the Mystic Arts (ep 4). Ident null, the same as the stephen-strange file: 'Doctor Strange' is his name and title. by-zombie-thanos.notes: Alien, the same as the MCU Thanos file (a Titan, not on the list); a zombie keeps their index. What If...? ep 5: his gauntlet lacks only the Mind Stone. by-zombie-captain-america.notes: A zombie keeps their index: Erskine's super soldier. Publicly Captain America. pr-st-awol.notes: Runaways: Anthony 'AWOL' Wall, Detective Flores's corrupt partner (played by Myles Bullock), who leads a strike team against the Runaways. No powers. fox-sentinels.notes: Days of Future Past: 'the Sentinel program is decommissioned'. cont follows the 'Secured' step (U.S. government); 'kept its robots' rests on the record's Apocalypse step (confiscated Sentinels used for training). Trask is part of the holder 'The Sentinel program', so he is not listed.

fox-dp-katanas.notes: origin null: the films never say where Wade got them. Only Wade is shown wielding them. cont null.

fox-dp-suit.notes: Deadpool (2016), Deadpool 2 (Cable puts Vanessa's Skee-Ball token in it over Wade's heart), Deadpool & Wolverine. Only Wade wears this suit. cont null.

fox-cable-time-device.notes: alsoHeld: in the Deadpool 2 mid-credits scene Negasonic and Yukio repair the device before handing it to Wade. Deadpool & Wolverine: Wade says he used it to reach the Avengers and then destroyed it (confirmed). cont null.

fox-dopinder-taxi.notes: Only Dopinder drives it; Wade, Colossus and Negasonic ride as passengers. cont null.

fox-anim-claws.notes: X-Men '97 S2 E5 'Weapon X, Lies, and DVDs' (July 2026, confirmed): at a Weapon X facility the adamantium process restores his claws. alsoHeld: Magneto magnetically rips the adamantium out of Wolverine's body on Asteroid M ('97 S1); this is pulling it out with his power rather than holding it in his hands, hence conf medium. cont null: no 'Secured' steps.

fox-anim-cerebro.notes: Everyone shown using it (Xavier, Jean) is Professor X or one of the holder 'The X-Men'. cont null: no 'Secured' steps.

fox-anim-master-mold.notes: alsoHeld: in X-Men '97 S1 the upgraded Master Mold attacks Genosha as part of Bastion's operation. Bastion is a holder in the Sentinels file but not in this one; it is a 'command' rather than 'hold', so conf medium. Gyrich co-built it in the 1992 series but is not shown operating it apart from Trask; left out. cont null.

fox-anim-blackbird.notes: Everyone shown flying it is Professor X or a member of the holder 'The X-Men'. Magneto rides it and shields it in 'The Final Decision' and later destroys one, but he does not fly it there; in X-Men '97 he leads the X-Men. I did not check the record's season 5 step (Magneto destroying it near Genosha). cont null.

fox-anim-magneto-helmet.notes: X-Men '97 S2 E4 (confirmed): Apocalypse atomizes Magneto in ancient Egypt, leaving only the helmet, which Xavier cradles and brings home. cont null: the 'Secured' step is Xavier keeping it, a person rather than an organization locking it away. origin null: neither series says who made it. I did not confirm that either series says it blocks telepathy, so props does not claim it. conf medium.

fox-anim-gambit-cards.notes: Confirmed: '97 S1 finale post-credits scene, Apocalypse picks up one of Gambit's cards in the ruins of Genosha; '97 S2 E7, X-Force finds Apocalypse's corpse and one of Gambit's cards in Athens. cont null: the 'Secured' steps are Apocalypse and X-Force picking up a single card, not an organization locking it away. No one else is shown holding them.

fox-anim-asteroid-m.notes: '97 S1 E10 (confirmed): Bastion aims to bring it down on Earth; Magneto pulls it away and it explodes in space. Everyone shown controlling it is already a holder. cont null.

fox-anim-ship.notes: X-Men '97 S2 (July-Aug 2026, confirmed). alsoHeld: E1-E2, in the far future the young Nathan (later Cable) merges with the Ship's computer and uses it to send the X-Men back to the 1990s; E4, Magneto pulls the Ship down with his power to plug a black hole, destroying it. Magneto is with the X-Men in Egypt, but he was not a named holder. Record check: the record skips Magneto destroying the Ship in E4 (it is later found abandoned in E9), and I could not confirm the '3000 B.C.' date. Beast (builds a time device from its parts) and Rogue are X-Men. cont null.

pr-bladesword.notes: alsoHeld: in Blade (1998) the vampire Crease grabs the sword and the hilt trap ruins his hand; in Blade II, Nomak kills himself with Blade's sword (Wikipedia: 'Nomak kills himself with Blade's sword'). Record check: the Blade II step names Blade as holder, but Nomak is the one holding it. I could not confirm whether Drake handles the sword in Blade: Trinity. origin null: the films never say who made it. cont null.

pr-glaive.notes: origin null: not stated on screen. props leaves out 'silver' (from the record) because I could not confirm the material. Deadpool & Wolverine: Blade's throwing glaive is part of his costume there, and he fights Azazel in the lair raid; I could not confirm that he kills Azazel with it. Only Blade wields it. cont null.

pr-blade-serum.notes: Blade (1998): Whistler's serum, Karen works to improve it. Blade: The Series: Shen makes it and Blade injects Krista (she receives it; she does not hold it). I could not confirm the record's Blade: Trinity inhaler step: plot summaries mention the Nightstalkers' rescue but no serum or inhaler. cont null.

pr-elektra-sai.notes: alsoHeld: Bullseye kills Elektra with one of her own sai in Daredevil (2003); the record's holder for that step is 'Nobody'. Elektra (2005): she kills Typhoid with her sai (confirmed). origin null: not stated. cont null.

pr-staff-of-one.notes: Runaways episode list: S1E5 Nico uses it to find Alex; S2E2 the kids take it from Tina; S2E11 Nico buries it; S3E2 Jonah finds it and breaks it; S3E4 Nico summons it and makes Jonah's family disappear. alsoHeld: Jonah (breaks it). cont null: the 'Secured' steps are Tina or Nico keeping it, not an organization.

pr-fistigons.notes: alsoHeld: S1E7 'Refraction': Victor attacks Chase with the Fistigons and is shot by Janet. A biker, 'Mike on a Bike', steals them in S2E1, but he is a passing thief, so I left him out. props: the show treats them as high-tech gauntlets; the comics' fire powers are not shown, so conf medium on the exact effect. cont null.

pr-jonah-ship.notes: Runaways S2E6-7: Jonah plans to unearth his ship and the Pride blow it up; S3E3: the new ship needs all four of the family; S3E4: Nico makes them vanish. cont null: the Pride dig for Jonah, but no one locks the ship away. conf medium because I did not confirm the exact on-screen description of where the ship came from.

sv-raimi-performance-enhancer.notes: cont null: the 'Secured' step is Harry finding his father's hidden storeroom, which is a person's stash, not an organization's containment. Only Norman and Harry are shown taking it.

sv-raimi-goblin-armor.notes: No one but Norman wears this armor (Harry's Spider-Man 3 gear is his own). cont null: the 'Secured' step is Harry's private storeroom.

sv-raimi-goblin-glider.notes: alsoHeld: in No Way Home the MCU's Peter, in a rage, raises the Goblin's glider to impale Norman; Tobey Maguire's Peter steps in and is stabbed in the back. Sources disagree on whether Tobey's Peter grabs the glider itself, so I did not list him. cont null: the 'Secured' step is Harry's storeroom.

sv-raimi-pumpkin-bombs.notes: alsoHeld: in Spider-Man 3 Peter throws a pumpkin bomb from Harry's glider at the symbiote (the record's holder for that step is 'Nobody'). cont null: the 'Secured' step is Harry's storeroom.

sv-raimi-spider-man-suit.notes: In Spider-Man 2 a garbage man brings the dumped suit to Jameson, and train passengers hand Peter his mask back, but none of them are named, so I left them out. cont null: the 'Secured' step is Jameson hanging it in his office, not an organization's containment.

sv-raimi-octavius-arms.notes: cont follows the No Way Home 'Secured' step. Peter repairs the inhibitor chip but never wields the arms. alsoHeld empty.

sv-asm-oscorp-spiders.notes: alsoHeld: in The Amazing Spider-Man 2, Harry forces Menken to inject him with the spider venom (Wikipedia). cont follows both 'Secured' (Oscorp) steps.

sv-asm-web-shooters.notes: Only Peter is shown wearing them. cont null.

sv-asm-spider-man-suit.notes: alsoHeld: on the Williamsburg Bridge in The Amazing Spider-Man, Peter takes off his mask and has the trapped boy, Jack, wear it so he'll be brave enough to climb to safety. Captain Stacy discovers Peter's identity when the police corner him, but I could not confirm that he pulls the mask off himself, so I left him out. cont null: the 'Secured' step is Peter setting the suit aside.

sv-itsv-collider.notes: alsoHeld: Olivia Octavius (Doc Ock) is the scientist who runs the collider for Fisk in Into the Spider-Verse; she operates it rather than holds it, so conf medium. Record check: Across the Spider-Verse, the Spot does reveal that his collider test brought over the spider from Earth-42 (Miguel later explains what it means). cont null.

sv-itsv-spider-42.notes: Confirmed: in Across the Spider-Verse the Spot reveals the collider test brought the spider from Earth-42. No one handles it. cont null.

sv-itsv-miles-suit.notes: Only Miles wears it. cont null.

sv-itsv-sp-dr.notes: Origin: Peni's intro line (Wikiquote): 'I have a psychic link with a spider who lives inside my father's robot'. quote null: that line is dialogue, not an inscription or enchantment. Across the Spider-Verse: an older Peni with a rebuilt SP//dr helps the Spider-Society (secondary sources). Only Peni pilots it. cont null.

sv-spider-society-watches.notes: Record check: in the Into the Spider-Verse post-credits scene Miguel says 'Let's start at the beginning, one last time. Earth-67' (Wikiquote and multiple outlets). The record's 'Earth-6799' looks wrong; it should be Earth-67. alsoHeld: at the end of Across, George Stacy hands Gwen a homemade portal watch Hobie left for her. That is Hobie's own build, not a Society watch, so I did not list him. Society members (Hobie, Jess, Pavitr, Peter B.) are under the holder 'Spider-Society'. I could not confirm whether Miles is given a watch at HQ, so he is not listed. cont null.

fox-juggernaut-helmet.notes: Deadpool & Wolverine (confirmed): Laura (X-23), who killed Juggernaut, throws his helmet up to Wade, who forces it onto Cassandra. After Pyro shoots her, Logan persuades Wade to take it off so she can heal. origin null: not stated. cont null.
